analysis:
The PR changes only documentation. In docs/developer/serving-performance-qualification.md, the "Last updated" date moves to 2026-10-21 and head lines 15-22 add a paragraph about deadline-admission estimator corrections (DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES). The paragraph says reviewed calibrations keep the per-row decode charge, and that no timing-catalog entry is needed. In docs/developer/test.md (head lines 113-138), a new "Deadline Admission Estimators" section lists synthetic test suites and swift test commands. The commands run scripted engines with no model, GPU or network, and the text states they do not qualify live refusal rates, hardware performance or routing.

I found no change to code, keys, attestation, encryption, the prefix cache (T-041), the WebSocket contract, or App Attest authorization (TB-011, T-052 to T-058). The docs do not weaken any stated qualification gate. They keep the deadline catalog empty, the unqualified legacy ceiling, and the requirement for independent evidence before a profile is promoted. No new trust boundary, secret exposure or authorization claim is introduced.

Open question for later passes: the head text claims behavior in the unsupplied code (DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES, the per-row decode charge, calibratedPathProven, and the architecture/inference.md#deadlines anchor). I cannot verify it, but it is documentation-only and does not affect a security conclusion. A further limitation is that test.md has only a patch excerpt, not full text, and the patch shows only additions.
